name: Cinematic multi-osc pad with formant/comb and slow FX motion
goal: Build a Weeknd-style cinematic pad: three analog basic-shape oscs with unison/detune (B −1 oct, high unison; C light unison), formant filter on C, comb filter on all, pad attack/release, free slow LFO→cutoff, then phaser→flanger→chorus→slow LFO-filtered FX→delay→reverb with restrained mixes.

source.title: HOW TO MAKE THE WEEKND CINEMATIC PAD | Serum 2 Sound Design Tutorial

prerequisites: Multi-osc synth with unison, formant and comb-like filters, phaser/flanger/chorus/delay/reverb

inputs.name: unison_profile
inputs.description: A moderate, B high (e.g. ~14), C low (~2)

constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided captions; do not invent UI or settings.
Original synthesis only — map brand UI (Serum/Vital/Pigments/Phase Plant/etc.) to portable osc/filter/FX roles for a browser or generic hybrid synth; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Prefer transferable signal-flow and motion relationships over vendor-specific preset names.
Style homage only — original parameters; do not copy named commercial presets.

steps.action: Osc A: analog basic shapes + unison/detune for width.
Osc B: same family, −1 octave, higher unison (tutorial ~14) + detune.
Osc C: light unison (~2) + detune; Filter1 formant-style on C only — set cutoff/resonance for vocal-like body.
Filter2 comb-minus (or comb) on A+B+C; set cutoff, resonance, drive.
Amp env: raise attack and release for pad.
Free slow LFO1 → filter cutoff(s) for movement.

FX: phaser (lower mix) → flanger (lower mix) → chorus (tweak delay/depth/mix down) → extra FX filter (low 24 dB) with very slow free LFO2 (e.g. 2 bars) unipolar to cutoff → delay → reverb; keep mixes moderate.

verification: Three-osc stack with B lower octave
FX mixes not at 100% washing the dry pad away
